title.en: Orthogonal projection and the residual vector

summary: Make the residual the visible subject: the shortest connection from a point to a subspace is perpendicular to it.
objective: Build a projection scene where I can move a point and a plane and confirm that the residual is perpendicular and minimal.
intent_signals: Show why the shortest distance to a plane is perpendicular to it.
Explain least squares as a projection in three dimensions.
example_prompts: Build an orthogonal projection demonstration with a movable point, a spanned plane and a residual readout.
Let me test other points in the plane and see that none is closer than the projection.
negative_signals: Not a regression modelling recipe: no data, fit statistics or inference.
Not a numerical solver comparison; conditioning and pivoting are out of scope.
not_for: Not a regression modelling recipe: no data, fit statistics or inference.
Not a numerical solver comparison; conditioning and pivoting are out of scope.

entities.name: Subspace
entities.guidance: Span the subspace from editable basis vectors and show them, so the plane is visibly generated rather than placed.

entities.name: Point and projection
entities.guidance: Draw the external point, its projection and the residual segment as three distinct objects with their own labels.

entities.name: Comparison probe
entities.guidance: Let a second point slide within the subspace with a live distance readout, so minimality can be tested instead of asserted.

state_contract.model: Editable spanning vectors from which an independent subset, or an orthonormal basis of their span, is selected with a stated rank tolerance; the reported subspace dimension is 2, 1 or 0. The external point, its projection and the residual follow from that basis, and the identity projection plus residual equals the point is checked numerically with a stated tolerance. The inverse formula A(A^T A)^-1 A^T is used only for the independent-column case.
state_contract.authority: The basis and the external point are authoritative; the projection, the residual and every distance readout are recomputed from them.
actions: Edit a basis vector, including making the two basis vectors parallel.
Slide the comparison probe inside the subspace.
Reset the basis, point and probe.

invariants: The residual is perpendicular to every vector in the subspace, not only to the drawn basis vectors.
No probe position inside the subspace produces a smaller distance than the projection.
Projecting an already projected point returns the same point.

What is drawn follows the reported dimension: a plane patch with a unique normal only in dimension 2, a line with a normal plane in dimension 1, and in dimension 0 the projection is the origin with the comparison probe fixed there.
motion_guidance: Animate the residual shrinking as the point approaches the subspace, and let it reach exactly zero when the point lies in it.
Do not animate the projection as a drop along a fixed screen axis; it must follow the subspace normal.
known_limits: Degenerate spanning sets collapse the subspace to a line or a point. The scene reports the dimension from a rank test with a stated tolerance and draws that case, rather than drawing a plane patch and a unique normal that do not exist.
Numeric tolerances make perpendicularity approximate in floating point.
Authored guidance only: no scene runtime, rendering or numerical calibration has been run for this recipe.

claims.statement: Any vector x can be written uniquely as the sum of its orthogonal projection onto a subspace W and a component in the orthogonal complement of W, and the projection is the closest vector to x in W with distance equal to the norm of that complement component.
claims.scope: Finite-dimensional real inner product space as presented in the cited section.

source_refs.locator: Interactive Linear Algebra 6.3, orthogonal decomposition and closest vector theorems

claims.statement: When W is the column space of a matrix A with linearly independent columns, orthogonal projection is given by the matrix A (A transpose A) inverse A transpose, and the projection transformation satisfies T composed with T equals T.
claims.scope: Independent-column case only; rank-deficient A requires a different construction.

source_refs.locator: Interactive Linear Algebra 6.3, projection matrix and idempotence

object_craft.structure: A bounded plane patch with a visible border and a normal marker rather than an infinite grid.
object_craft.material: Low-opacity fill with an opaque border so points behind the plane remain visible and depth stays readable.
object_craft.articulation: The patch is regenerated whenever a basis vector changes.

object_craft.structure: Two markers of different shapes joined by the residual segment with a right-angle glyph at the plane.
object_craft.material: A single accent for the residual, reserved so nothing else in the scene competes with it.
object_craft.articulation: All three rebuild from the current basis and point.

physical_contract.scope: Mathematical construction and measurement; no physical meaning is attached to the vectors.
checks: Projection plus residual reconstructs the original point within the stated tolerance.
The comparison probe never reports a smaller distance than the projection.
